target_customer: Consumers in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia who book rides and order food and groceries, plus drivers, couriers and merchants on the supply side
problem: Algerian and wider Maghreb cities lacked reliable, transparent on-demand rides and delivery, and digital payments were underdeveloped.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on rides and deliveries, expanding into fintech services such as payments and credit

founders.name: Noureddine Tayebi
founders.background_notes: Cairoscene describes him as an ex Silicon Valley professional; the YC page shows no background and a Bloomberg headline in its news list mentions a Stanford alum without naming which founder. Spelling varies (Tayeb, Tayebi).

founders.name: El Mahdi Yettou
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by YC and Cairoscene; no background found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Careem
competitors.what: Ride-hailing service that entered Algiers in 2019
competitors.traction_then: Described by March 2020 coverage as Yassir's most serious competitor in Algeria

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard ride and delivery marketplace engineering (dispatch, maps, payments) but built for low connectivity, cash-heavy Maghreb markets with taxi regulation.

defensibility.rationale: Local two-sided network of drivers and riders and local operations know-how, but global players such as Uber and Careem could enter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Careem entered Algiers in 2019 and left Algeria in 2022 per a 2025 industry overview, while Yassir kept growing and raised later rounds.

market_need_then: Informal taxis and weak digital services in North African cities; March 2020 coverage shows a contested ride-hailing market in Algeria.

branding.name_origin: Yassir is an Arabic given name linked to the root meaning ease or prosperity; no company source states why it was chosen.
branding.domain_note: Uses yassir.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.visual_style: Marketing site presents a unified all in one super app with trilingual pages (English, French, Arabic)
identity.voice_and_tone: Convenience, safety and fair pricing; values listed as ambition, transparency and trust, quality, performance

brand_strength.rationale: A regional super app brand with 8 million plus users reported by funding coverage, but no source found on brand-driven virality or press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Super app adding delivery, grocery and financial services
pivots.why: YC page says the company built on its ride and delivery infrastructure to introduce payments, savings and borrowing

outcome_analysis: Yassir became one of the best funded YC companies from Africa, raising a $30M Series A in late 2021 and a $150M Series B in November 2022 led by BOND, and later reported more than 8 million users across six countries. It expanded from rides into delivery and fintech and acquired adtech firm Kawarizmi in March 2026. Rival Careem left Algeria in 2022. No failure signals were found.
notes: Seed of $13.25M comes from Techloy and FoodBusinessMEA only and has no date or investor list, so treat the amount as lightly verified. Total raised of about $193.25M after the Series B is stated in coverage, implying seed plus Series A near 43M. Series A date is inferred from Techloy and Crunchbase wording about nearly 12 months before the Series B. Seedtable lists a Series A of 37.4M but labels its splits as estimates, ignored. Maghreb Emergent and Financial Afrik headlines in March 2020 about Uber, Careem and Yassir conflict on who bought whom; no acquisition of Yassir is confirmed anywhere else, so no exit is recorded. Founder education and prior employers were not found in opened sources.
